criteria.criterion: Central passenger service between Paddington low level/Paddington and Abbey Wood commenced by December 2018
required_elements: Crossrail/Elizabeth line central passenger service commenced
service was between Paddington low level/Paddington and Abbey Wood
criteria.promise_scope: Crossrail promised that Crossrail services would commence in December 2018 in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood. Beneficiaries are the passengers who would use that central section; location is specified as Paddington low level to Abbey Wood.
criteria.observed_scope: TfL evidence shows the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood did not open in December 2018, was deferred to Autumn 2019, and later operated as the Elizabeth line between Paddington and Abbey Wood by May 2022. The observed operating service is on the same central corridor, but the delivered opening date shown is later than December 2018.
criteria.explanation: The original undertaking is explicit: 'December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood' (c1). Later evidence directly contradicts opening by that date: 'The Crossrail Ltd Board took the decision to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 on 29 August 2018' (c2), showing December 2018 was no longer the opening date before it arrived. Operational evidence then shows the service running much later as the Elizabeth line, including service details between Paddington and Abbey Wood (c3) and journeys on the opening day of the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood (c4). Together, the sources establish that the central passenger service eventually opened on that corridor, but not by the originally planned December 2018 date.

trace.label: REFUTED
trace.verdict: The December 2018 opening commitment is documented, but the evidence refutes that it opened by that date. The central Paddington-to-Abbey Wood passenger service was deferred and later opened as the Elizabeth line well after December 2018.
trace.reasoning:
Requested scope: Did London's Elizabeth line open its central passenger service from Paddington to Abbey Wood by the originally planned December 2018 date?

The question asks about the exact original undertaking: commencement of Crossrail central services between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood in December 2018. Citation c1 documents that promise. Citation c2 directly shows the opening date was changed before December 2018, with the board deciding on 29 August 2018 to open the central section in Autumn 2019 instead. Citations c3 and c4 show the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood was in operation later as the Elizabeth line, confirming eventual delivery of the corridor service but also confirming it was not open by the original December 2018 target. Because the requested outcome is opening by the originally planned date, and the sources directly show a later opening trajectory incompatible with that date, the claim is refuted rather than merely unverified.

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood”
https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/annual-update-on-crossrail-2017

c2: “The Crossrail Ltd Board took the decision to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 on 29 August 2018.”
https://tfl.gov.uk/corporate/transparency/freedom-of-information/foi-request-detail?referenceId=FOI-1470-1819

c3: “The Elizabeth line will operate 12 trains per hour between Paddington and Abbey Wood from Monday to Saturday 06:30 to 23:00.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-elizabeth-line-to-open-on-24-may-2022

c4: “The celebratory response to the opening saw around 260,000 journeys made on the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood across its opening day, clearly showing its popularity.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-celebrations-as-transformational-elizabeth-line-begins-operations
